items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: that Ralph Bunch graduated from in the first graduation class

ctx.x: Growing up in Los Angeles. Well, I don't know. Los Angeles was quite a different place from what it is now. When I came up, my neighborhood was completely mixed up with just about a potpourri of every race that you could ever think about, because Los Angeles, when I came here, didn't have a lot of people in 1918. It was sort of like a oasis sitting out in this part of the world out here.

All of my friends that I went to school with were all mixed up races. There were many, many Jewish people, many Mexicans, a few Indians, Irish and Assyrians and there were Russians, just a whole mix-up of everything. The school that I went to, the high school that I went to at that time, had about ten percent blacks in it. That high school today is 100 percent black, Jefferson High School. It's the same school, as a matter of fact, that Ralph Bunch graduated from in the first graduation class, I think around…
Jefferson had a lot of illustrious alumni, hasn't it?
